messages:
Priya Patel: Hey support — customers hitting our /v1/rerank endpoint are getting 429s all afternoon. Error body says `quota_exceeded` and `rate_limit` with Retry-After sometimes, but other calls fail with no Retry-After header. We're seeing this on prod only, started ~10:15 PDT. Impacting a handful of big customers. Help? :pray:

Jessie Gomez: Sorry you're seeing that, Priya. Can you paste a sample request (headers + body) and the full error response? Also which customer/org id so I can correlate logs.

Priya Patel: Sample (sanitized):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwrk-large","queries":["q1","q2"],"candidates":[["a","b","c"]],"top_k":5}'

Error JSON returned: `{\n  "error": "quota_exceeded",\n  "message": "per_route_quota_exceeded: rerank_concurrent_requests",\n  "code": 429\n}`

Customer org: org_0xA7F (big ecommerce integration).

Jessie Gomez: Thanks. I'm pulling logs now. Are they sending large batch sizes or a lot of small concurrent calls? Rerank has stricter concurrency/throughput controls than text-gen.

rerank-bot: [alert] route=/v1/rerank status=429 rate_limit_key=org_0xA7F window=60s count=78 limit=60

Arjun Rao: I can see spikes from that org. Traffic pattern: many parallel short-lived connections at ~10:12–10:18, peaks hitting ~120 rps for rerank route from two IPs. Gateway applied per-organization token bucket and started 429s when bucket drained. Some responses include `Retry-After: 5` but not all — looks like a race between gateway and runtime fallback.

Marta Liu: Is this a quota or a bug? We do have a per-route quota for rerank to protect KV cache and CPU. If they exceeded that, 429 is expected. But the missing Retry-After is odd. Could be because requests got to the runtime directly bypassing gateway?

Jessie Gomez: Priya — did they recently deploy a client change? Any naive retry loops or fanout logic?

Priya Patel: The customer says they ramped a new batcher to parallelize across 16 workers. Their client does simple fixed-interval retries, no jitter. They also increased `top_k` to 64 last night for better accuracy.

Arjun Rao: That explains it. Rerank with large `top_k` increases CPU per call and reduces throughput; combined with aggressive parallelization, they blew through per-org quotas. Gateway observed bursts and returned 429s. The missing Retry-After may be from the runtime when we cut connections mid-processing.

Jessie Gomez: Quick mitigation options:
- Ask customer to reduce concurrency and batch size (set top_k <= 16)
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter and honour `Retry-After`
- We can temporarily bump their per-route quota from 60 req/min to 600 req/min while they stabilize
- Route them to dedicated capacity if they need consistent throughput

Priya Patel: Customer asked for immediate action — they claim business-critical traffic. Can we bump quota now?

Arjun Rao: I can apply a temporary lift for org_0xA7F for 2 hours. Will update rate-limit config in gateway: `rate_limit.org:org_0xA7F.routes.rerank = 600/min` (ephemeral). Doing it now.

rerank-bot: [action] rate-limit update applied for org=org_0xA7F route=/v1/rerank new_limit=600 window=60s by=Arjun Rao TTL=7200s

Jessie Gomez: Priya, let the customer know we applied a temporary increase for 2h. They should also: add exponential backoff, add jitter, cap concurrency, and reduce top_k. We'll monitor.

Priya Patel: Relayed — they accepted the temporary lift and will throttle client ASAP. Thanks!

Marta Liu: Follow-ups for eng/docs: we should clarify in rerank docs the per-route quotas and call out `top_k` and batch-size impact on throughput. Also add example client retry code that respects 429 + Retry-After and uses backoff + jitter.

Jessie Gomez: Agreed. Action items:
- Arjun: monitor metrics and revert or extend ephemeral quota (ETA: watch 2h)
- Marta: update docs + sample retry snippet (ETA: EOD)
- Support (Jessie/Priya): send customer postmortem + recommended client changes (ETA: 1 business day)

Arjun Rao: Quick note on reproducible steps for SRE/ENG if needed:
1) Repro from staging: run parallel `ab`/wrk clients against /v1/rerank with `top_k=64` and 64 concurrent connections. Expect to hit per-route bucket and see 429s.
2) Grab gateway logs with `kubectl logs -l app=api-gateway -c ratelimiter | grep org_0xA7F`
3) Check runtime traces: `grep X-Request-ID` from runtime logs to find requests that were killed mid-processing.

Priya Patel: One more customer request — they want an explanation for unexpected scores when some rerank calls returned partial results due to 429 mid-run. Is that expected?

Marta Liu: Partial or empty rerank responses can happen when runtime preempts expensive jobs. We should document that `status=429` can come with an empty `rankings` array. Recommend client treat that as a soft failure and retry with backoff and reduced `top_k`/batch.

Jessie Gomez: Closing loop: Arjun will post metrics update in this thread when the lift is reverted or extended. Support will send customer followup. Any objections?

Arjun Rao: No objections. I'll check back at +30m increments. :thumbsup:

rerank-bot: [note] metrics: org_0xA7F rerank 1m avg before lift=78/min after lift=42/min now=40/min

Jessie Gomez: Thanks team. Marking resolved for now; re-open if errors reappear. :white_check_mark:
